description:

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect.

no news reports later confirmed that 77 year old juan was innocent in teresa's death however investigators quickly focused in on his 42 year old son john surveillance footage allegedly shows john driving into the neighborhood and pulling teresa's unconscious body from his truck and onto the road after an alleged violent domestic dispute because radio The traffic indicated she was still breathing when police arrived. It is believed she is still alive at this moment. John then runs her over, goes to his father's house to pick him up and returns 35 minutes later to stage the discovery of Teresa. It is assumed Juan is unaware of what he is about to witness. Both John and Juan wait several minutes for police to arrive. It is apparent that Juan is the individual making the 911 call. Just seconds before police pull up on scene, John runs away towards his father's home. Outside of video evidence, officers also discovered brain matter on the tire. Teresa also had black hairs under her fingernails, which likely matched John's scratches. indicating a struggle. After his arrest, John Robert Galvan was charged with one count of reckless driving and causing death, one count of homicide by manslaughter with a motor vehicle, one count of failure to stop at the scene of an accident when at fault, and causing death, and one count of driving with a suspended license and causing death. He was held on a half-million dollar bail. Sources indicate that over two years later, he was found guilty and sentenced on, one count of reckless driving and causing death, and one count of homicide by manslaughter with a motor vehicle. All other charges were dismissed. Michigan sentencing uses a range rather than a fixed term, and in this case, John received a sentence of five years and six months to 15 years in prison, becoming eligible to request parole after five years and six months, though it is very unlikely to be granted. This is because he was previously granted parole following a 2011 drunk driving case. In that case, he crashed into the vehicle of off-duty Highland Park police officer came in bowed at over 100 miles per hour. Despite wearing a seatbelt, the off-duty officer was ejected from her vehicle. Her pelvis was crushed, her neck was broken, her spleen was removed, her lung collapsed, a stroke was triggered, and she was put in a three-week coma. Witnesses from that incident told investigators they saw John trying to throw away liquor bottles before police arrived at the scene to arrest him for the 7 a.m. near fatal crash. In the years after the crash, he continues to receive impaired driving charges and in 11 years only paid $1,000 of the $38,000 restitution he owed. Officer Bode shared her thoughts about John's recent homicide charges on local news. If you asked me how I feel him, I think he didn't. He didn't care. I have a feeling if you let him out. I don't feel like he cares about anybody else. I knew it. I knew, I knew it. And then I just couldn't believe it. And my heart goes out to that lady and her family. As officers discovered in this video, John is also a registered sex offender. He was found guilty for second-degree criminal sexual conduct on a person under the age of 13 in 1999 when he was 20 years old. Reports indicate he spent a seven-year prison sentence for that crime. Assuming John serves his full sentence, he will not be released until February 13, 2037, exactly 15 years after he killed 42-year-old. Teresa Sanchez. He will be 57 years old when released.

with a motor vehicle. All other charges were dismissed. Michigan sentencing uses a range
rather than a fixed term, and in this case, John received a sentence of five years and six months
to 15 years in prison, becoming eligible to request parole after five years and six months,
though it is very unlikely to be granted. This is because he was previously granted parole
following a 2011 drunk driving case. In that case, he crashed into the vehicle of off-duty
Highland Park police officer came in bowed at over 100 miles per hour. Despite wearing a seatbelt,
the off-duty officer was ejected from her vehicle. Her pelvis was crushed, her neck was
broken, her spleen was removed, her lung collapsed, a stroke was triggered, and she was put in a
three-week coma. Witnesses from that incident told investigators they saw John trying to throw away
liquor bottles before police arrived at the scene to arrest him for the 7 a.m. near fatal crash. In the
years after the crash, he continues to receive impaired driving charges and in 11 years only paid
